business.about: HDFC Bank Limited (also known as HDFC) is an Indian banking and financial services company headquartered in Mumbai. It is India's largest private sector bank by assets and the world's tenth-largest bank by market capitalization as of May 2024. As of April 2024, HDFC Bank has a market capitalization of $145 billion, making it the third-largest company on the Indian stock exchanges. [1]
business.in_their_words: Total AUM grew 15.3% year- on-year, including a 1.9% impact of FCNR (B) leverage, with SME and retail assets leading the charge. Our industry-leading asset quality metrics reflect the top-quartile credit quality choices we have consistently made. HDFC Bank has always incorporated cutting- edge technologies into its operations, and we are now bringing AI into the heart of how the bank operates. While leaving this organization is an emotional moment for me personally, I take comfort in the fact that I'm leaving behind a solid platform, which has demonstrated strength and resilience to navigate regulatory embargoes, an unprecedented COVID event, a large, complex merger when the economic outlook warranted monetary tightening, and other governance matters of the recent past having been settled completely. calls: Growth is accelerating: revenue CAGR 26.9% over 3y vs 22.1% over 5y
Margins compressing: -12% latest vs 7% average of prior years
Adequate cash conversion: 5-yr operating cash flow is 0.89× reported profit

items.speaker: Sashidhar Jagdishan
items.quote: The pace of retail disbursements is accelerating and has crossed Rs 90,000 crores during Q2 FY27 as against Rs 76,000 crores in Q1 of this year.

items.speaker: Sashidhar Jagdishan
items.quote: As you will see in our published deck, CASA grew at about 10.8% on an overall basis.

items.speaker: Sashidhar Jagdishan
items.quote: Our ECLGS disbursals of Rs 41,000 crores were highest across all banks as of August 26, when the scheme achieved targeted levels.

items.speaker: Srinivasan Vaidyanathan
items.quote: And so, if you look at our total deposits, branch-driven deposits is at about 80% or so of the total, which is on one of those pages that we have published, you will see that.

items.speaker: Srinivasan Vaidyanathan
items.quote: One is I do want to mention that the borrowing mix which is at 11%, we don't expect that it will just settle at 8% or 9%, right?

items.speaker: Srinivasan Vaidyanathan
items.quote: I don't think there will be anything material, but there will be some because as exactly I described, standard assets today are approximately 40, there are some 25 basis points, some 100 basis points, but on an average 40 basis points standard assets.

items.speaker:
Thank you. 
Srinivasan Vaidyanathan
items.quote: If you just replace borrowings with time deposit or you envisage to replace with a mix of time and CASA, but only time little more than 100 basis points you will see.

items.speaker: Sashidhar Jagdishan
items.quote: At least if you see through large part of FY26, the nominal GDP growth expected was somewhere around the 9%, 9.5%, so one consensus until the large part of the year was a system credit growth of around 10.5% to 11.5%.

items.speaker: Sashidhar Jagdishan
items.quote: In fact, the less than INR 3 crores deposits have grown, which has been mobilized in 2026 on a net basis, has grown up almost about 74% over the net incremental deposits for FY25 on that less than INR 3 crores bucket.

items.speaker: Sashidhar Jagdishan
items.quote: It is something that we have to navigate, but it's not too far away from the momentum we have seen from a 5.4% growth in FY25 to a 12% growth.

items.speaker: Srinivasan Vaidyanathan
items.quote: Seshadri, if you look at the cost growth that we have, we have seen that at a level almost at, call it, 6.5%, 7% or so is the full year, right?

items.speaker: Sashidhar Jagdishan
items.quote: So what constituted 31% of the total net accretion in FY25 now constitutes 47%.

items.speaker: Kaizad Bharucha
items.quote: A thing I had mentioned in the past, which had come up and that continues to hold good as the book matures, as the engagement matures, that the average balances that we see of customers that keep their liability with us who have their home loan goes up 2x to 2.25x compared to the standard average balances that would otherwise be witnessed in the banks.

items.speaker: Sashidhar Jagdishan
items.quote: And then maybe by FY '27, by the natural growth and even with the growth in the way we are expecting in terms of faster growth rate, I think we should land somewhere around the 85% to 90% for FY '27.

items.speaker: Kaizad Bharucha
items.quote: So our understanding as of now is next year, we expect system growth to be between 12% to 13%, when you look at nominal GDP and the credit growth that's required to support nominal GDP.

items.speaker: Sashidhar Jagdishan
items.quote: We said we will try and be in a range of somewhere between 90% to 96% in the year FY '26, which is what we will be is what we are very confident about.

items.speaker: Sashidhar Jagdishan
items.quote: Practically speaking, it will be somewhere, if 90% is that range, then somewhere around the 90% is something that we'll be happy with.

items.speaker: Kaizad Bharucha
items.quote: So if we're talking about 12% to 13%, we are talking about a couple of percentage points above that going into the next year.

items.speaker: Srinivasan Vaidyanathan
items.quote: For card customers spending on their card account and having 100 outstanding, at the aggregate level in the bank, we see almost north of 5.5x deposit balances from the customers.
